fields.title: Erectile dysfunction
fields.bodyHtml:
Erectile dysfunction: understanding, diagnosis, treatment and the advantages of treatment in Israel

Introduction

Erectile dysfunction, also known as impotence, is a common medical condition in men in which it is difficult to achieve or maintain an erection sufficient for intercourse. It can seriously affect quality of life and relationships between partners. In this article we look at the methods of diagnosing and treating erectile dysfunction and the advantages of having it treated in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis begins with a detailed discussion with the doctor about the patient's symptoms and medical history. The doctor's main task is to establish the possible causes and draw up the best treatment plan. The main diagnostic methods are:

  • Medical history and physical examination: the doctor interviews the patient to identify risk factors and possible causes, and carries out a physical examination to detect any abnormalities.
  • Hormone testing: erectile dysfunction may be linked to a hormonal imbalance. Measuring testosterone and other hormones can help establish the cause.
  • Testing for diabetes: diabetes may be one of the causes, so blood glucose may be measured.
  • Ultrasound examination: may be carried out to assess the blood supply to the genital organs.

Methods of treatment

Treatment may involve several approaches, and the choice depends on the cause and severity of the condition. The main treatments are:

  • Lifestyle changes: in some cases erectile dysfunction is linked to the way a person lives. The doctor may recommend changes to diet, more physical activity and reducing stress.
  • Medicines to improve erections: drugs such as sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis) and vardenafil (Levitra) may be prescribed to improve blood flow to the genital organs and help achieve an erection.
  • Injections or medicines administered into the urethra: the doctor may recommend injections into the penis or medicines placed in the urethra to improve erections.
  • Penile prosthesis: where other treatments are ineffective, surgical fitting of a penile prosthesis may be needed.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the leading countries in the treatment of erectile dysfunction, offering patients high-quality medical services and advanced technology. Treatment in Israel offers the following advantages:

  • Experienced specialists: medical centres in Israel work with highly qualified doctors and surgeons who specialise in this field and have extensive experience and knowledge.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel understand how important it is to treat every patient individually. They take account of the medical history and the patient's particular circumstances and needs in drawing up the best treatment plan.
  • Innovative treatments: medical centres in Israel use advanced treatments, including innovative medicines and surgical techniques.
  • Confidentiality and comfort: patients who come to Israel for treatment can count on a high level of confidentiality and comfort during their stay.

Conclusion

Erectile dysfunction is a common medical condition that can be treated successfully by various means, including lifestyle changes, medication and surgery. Treatment in Israel offers patients a wide choice of options and a high level of medical expertise. If you have problems with erections, it is important to consult a qualified specialist for professional help and to determine the best treatment plan for a full and satisfying sexual life.

fields.title: Patient-specific joint planning
fields.bodyHtml:
Patient-specific joint planning: an innovative approach in Israeli orthopaedics

Patient-specific joint planning is an advanced approach in orthopaedics based on the use of personalised implants and technologies to achieve the most precise and effective joint replacement possible. In Israel this method is beginning to play a key part in the surgical treatment of joint disease and injury, allowing patients to restore joint function and quality of life to a new standard.

How the method works

Patient-specific joint planning involves creating unique implants and surgical instruments fully adapted to the anatomy of each individual patient. This is achieved through careful prior analysis of MRI and CT images of the joint, on the basis of which specialised software creates a precise three-dimensional model of the future implant and a plan for the operation.

Advantages of patient-specific joint planning

  • High precision and fit
    Implants are created individually for every patient. They fit perfectly and match the anatomical structures of the joint as closely as possible.
  • Shorter operations and recovery
    The precision of preparation and planning shortens the operation and speeds recovery afterwards.
  • Minimised risk of complications
    Individual planning reduces the likelihood of implant rejection and of infection and other complications after surgery.
  • Better functional results
    Patients report a greater degree of restored joint function and greater satisfaction with the results of surgery.

Where the method is used

Patient-specific joint planning is used successfully in the replacement of various joints, including the knee, hip and ankle. The approach is particularly valuable in complex cases where standard implants cannot provide the necessary precision and function.

Leading clinics and specialists

Many leading clinics in Israel have already introduced patient-specific joint planning into their practice. Israel has highly qualified specialists and modern equipment for this. Every patient can count on a detailed consultation and a comprehensive approach to treatment.

Patient-specific joint planning in Israel opens new prospects. Patients with joint disease and injury are offered a higher standard of personalised medical care and a better chance of recovery.

fields.title: Myocardial infarction
fields.bodyHtml:
Myocardial infarction: advanced treatment in Israel

A myocardial infarction, or heart attack, is an acute condition caused by a disruption of the blood supply to the heart muscle, which damages the heart tissue. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive approach to the treatment and rehabilitation of patients after a heart attack, using the most modern technologies and techniques.

Diagnosis of myocardial infarction:

  1. Electrocardiogram (ECG): the main tool for diagnosing a heart attack quickly.
  2. Laboratory tests: measurement of cardiac markers (troponins, CK-MB) in the blood, which indicate damage to the heart muscle.
  3. Echocardiography: ultrasound examination to assess the function of the heart and detect areas where the walls move less well.
  4. Coronary angiography: an invasive investigation that allows the coronary arteries to be seen and areas of narrowing or blockage identified.

Methods of treating myocardial infarction:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents to prevent blood clots forming.
    • Beta blockers, ACE inhibitors and statins to reduce the load on the heart, improve its function and lower the risk of a further heart attack.
  2. Interventional treatment:
    • Stenting: a catheter with a balloon at its tip is passed into the vessel and guided to the narrowed section. The balloon is inflated to widen the narrowing, after which a stent — a metal mesh — is placed in the vessel to hold the artery open and maintain normal blood flow.
    • Coronary artery bypass grafting: an operation that creates a bypass route for blood to reach the part of the heart receiving too little because the coronary arteries are blocked. The patient's own vein or artery is used to create a graft that bypasses the blocked section.
  3. Rehabilitation:
    • Covers a range of measures, from exercise and changes to diet through to psychological support. These programmes aim to aid recovery after a heart attack, improve general health and prevent further cardiovascular disease.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: every treatment plan is drawn up with the patient's personal needs and state of health in mind.
  • An interdisciplinary team: cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, rehabilitation specialists and others take part in treatment.
  • Access to innovative treatments: patients have access to the most modern stenting and bypass technologies, including biocompatible stents and minimally invasive surgical techniques.
  • A high standard of post-operative care and rehabilitation: particular attention is given to recovery after treatment, which helps patients return to normal life quickly.

Treatment of myocardial infarction in Israel combines effectiveness and safety with a focus on restoring heart function as fully as possible and improving patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Stroke (ischaemic and haemorrhagic)
fields.bodyHtml:
Ischaemic stroke: advanced treatment in Israel

Diagnosis of ischaemic stroke:

  • Medical examination and history taking.
  • Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain.
  • Echocardiography to assess the work of the heart and identify possible sources of clots.
  • Doppler examination of the vessels of the neck and brain.
  • Laboratory blood tests.

Treatment of ischaemic stroke:

  • Thrombolytic therapy to dissolve the clot that blocked the vessel.
  • Anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy to prevent new clots.
  • In rare cases stenting of the vessels of the brain may be recommended to restore blood flow.
  • Early rehabilitation, including physiotherapy and speech and language therapy.

Haemorrhagic stroke: an integrated approach to treatment in Israel

Diagnosis of haemorrhagic stroke:

  • Medical examination and history.
  • Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to identify the bleeding.
  • Echocardiography to assess the risk of cardioembolic bleeding.
  • Angiography to assess the vessels of the brain and find the source of the bleeding.
  • Laboratory tests, including clotting studies.

Treatment of haemorrhagic stroke:

  • Control of blood pressure to minimise the risk of further bleeding.
  • Surgery to deal with the source of the bleeding, for example removal of a haematoma or reinforcement of a vessel wall.
  • Neurosurgical operations where urgent intervention is needed to reduce pressure inside the skull.
  • Rehabilitation aimed at restoring lost function and adjusting to changes in daily life after a stroke.

Treatment and rehabilitation after a stroke in Israel involve individual programmes based on the latest research and clinical experience, which gives patients the best possible recovery and a return to an active life.
